family_title: Prompts, prefixes and learned states (soft-context adaptation)

methods.name: Prompt Tuning
methods.paper_title: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning
methods.formula_latex: \Pr_{\theta;\,\theta_P}\big(Y \mid [P;\,X_e]\big),\quad P\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d}\ \text{trained},\quad X_e=\mathrm{Embed}_{\theta}(X)\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d};\ \ \theta\ (\text{every } W_0)\ \text{frozen}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence (layer 0 only)
methods.structure: A free \ell\times d matrix of virtual-token embeddings concatenated in front of the input embedding sequence; the states of the prompt positions in deeper layers are not free but are computed by the frozen network from P (in a causal decoder they depend on P alone, so prompt tuning is prefix-tuning with the per-layer prefixes constrained to the frozen network's own image of P).
methods.mergeable_reason: The prompt lengthens every sequence by \ell tokens and cannot be absorbed into W_0; at best its per-layer keys/values can be pre-computed and served as a cached prefix.
methods.identity_at_init: No exact identity: prepending any tokens redistributes attention. Initialization options are random, sampled vocabulary embeddings, or embeddings of the class-label (verbalizer) tokens; HF PEFT exposes TEXT / SAMPLE_VOCAB / RANDOM.
methods.key_idea: Replace the discrete prompt by ℓ continuous 'virtual token' embeddings that are the only trainable parameters; the gap to full fine-tuning closes as the frozen model grows, so a single frozen model can serve many tasks with tiny per-task prompts.
methods.results_note: With LM-adapted T5, prompt tuning becomes competitive with scale and at T5-XXL (11B) matches model tuning (including the multi-task baseline) on SuperGLUE, while transferring better zero-shot to domain shifts.

relations.note: Li & Liang's 'embedding-only' ablation; only the layer-0 prefix is free, deeper prefixes are induced by the frozen network.
P-Tuning with identity prompt encoder and all virtual tokens placed at the front.
Shallow (input-only) instance of deep prompt tuning.
Standard additive-weight baseline; prompt tuning uses orders of magnitude fewer parameters but needs scale.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2104.08691 (Lester, 2021-04) and ACL Anthology 2021.emnlp-main.243 confirmed; formula matches Sec. 2; HF PromptTuningConfig (init TEXT/SAMPLE_VOCAB/RANDOM) confirmed in peft main (v0.21.1).

methods.name: Prefix-Tuning
methods.paper_title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation
methods.formula_latex: h_i=\begin{cases}P_\theta[i,:] & i\in P_{\mathrm{idx}}\\ \mathrm{LM}_\phi(z_i,h_{<i}) & \text{otherwise}\end{cases}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \mathrm{head}^{(l)}=\mathrm{Attn}\big(XW_q^{(l)},\,[P_k^{(l)};XW_k^{(l)}],\,[P_v^{(l)};XW_v^{(l)}]\big),\ \ P_k^{(l)},P_v^{(l)}\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d},\ l=1,\dots,L;\ \ \text{training: } P_\theta[i,:]=\mathrm{MLP}_\theta(P'_\theta[i,:]),\ P'_\theta\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times k};\ \ \phi\ (W_0)\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 2L\ell d\ \text{(stored, one key and one value prefix per attention layer of a decoder-only LM; an encoder-decoder prefixes each attention stack)};\ \ \ell k+|\mathrm{MLP}_\theta|\ \text{during training (MLP discarded afterwards)}
methods.locus: keys/values at every attention layer (decoder; encoder and decoder for enc-dec models in the paper)
methods.structure: Learned key/value vectors prepended at every layer, i.e. a learned initial KV-cache state of length \ell. By He et al. (2022) this is equivalently a gated parallel attention-adapter: h \leftarrow (1-\lambda(x))\,h+\lambda(x)\,\mathrm{softmax}(xW_qP_k^\top)P_v, with gate \lambda(x) = attention mass on the prefix.
methods.mergeable_reason: The prefix adds \ell extra key/value slots to every attention layer (extra attention cost per token); it can be served as a cached prefix but not folded into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: No exact identity: any prefix diverts attention mass \lambda(x)>0 away from the content. HF PEFT's init_weights='zero' zeroes keys and values, which still rescales attention outputs by 1-\lambda(x). Li & Liang initialize the prefix with activations of real (preferably task-relevant) words, which substantially helps in low-data settings; direct optimization of P is unstable, hence the MLP reparametrization.
methods.key_idea: Optimize a short continuous 'context' that every token can attend to at every layer, steering a frozen LM like a prompt would but with far more expressive power than input embeddings alone (discrete prompt < embedding-only < prefix-tuning).
methods.results_note: With 0.1% of parameters, GPT-2 prefix-tuning is comparable to fine-tuning on table-to-text (E2E, WebNLG, DART), outperforms it in low-data settings and extrapolates better to unseen categories, but trails full fine-tuning on XSUM summarization with BART.

relations.note: Prompt tuning only frees the layer-0 slice of the prefix.
P-Tuning v2 is the same deep-prompt parameterization with an NLU-oriented recipe (optional reparametrization, classification head).
He et al. (2022) rewrite prefix-tuning as a parallel adapter with W_1=W_qP_k^⊤, W_2=P_v, softmax nonlinearity and input-dependent gate λ(x).
Cartridges are prefix-tuning without the MLP reparametrization, trained by context distillation.
On S4 SSMs every prefix acts only through an initial-state update (Galim et al., Prop. 1); initial-state tuning is an upper bound, equal when \ell \ge H under a genericity condition.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2101.00190 and 2021.acl-long.353 confirmed; Eq. (3) and the MLP reparametrization P_theta[i,:]=MLP(P'_theta[i,:]) (k=512/800) checked in Sec. 4.2-4.3. HF PrefixTuningConfig confirmed; its PrefixEncoder (adapted from the P-tuning-v2 code) uses a Linear-Tanh-Linear projection when prefix_projection=True, and prefixes only the decoder of seq2seq models.
corrections: trainable_params: clarified that 2L\ell d counts one K/V prefix per attention stack (Li & Liang prefix both encoder and decoder for BART)

relations[initial-state-tuning]: type changed equivalent-to -> special-case-of: Galim et al. Prop. 1 shows prefix-tuning on S4 is realised by an initial state, with the converse only when prefix length >= H (generic case); Kang et al. call initial-state tuning an upper bound on prefix-tuning

methods.name: P-Tuning
methods.full_name: P-Tuning (continuous prompts with a prompt encoder)
methods.paper_title: GPT Understands, Too
methods.formula_latex: T=\{[P_{0:i}],\,x,\,[P_{i+1:j}],\,y,\,[P_{j+1:k}]\}\ \longmapsto\ \{h_0,\dots,h_i,\,e(x),\,h_{i+1},\dots,h_j,\,e(y),\,h_{j+1},\dots,h_k\},\quad (h_0,\dots,h_k)=f_\psi(P_0,\dots,P_k)\ \ (f_\psi:\ \text{LSTM or MLP prompt encoder});\ \ P,\psi\ \text{trained, LM frozen (or tuned)}
methods.trainable_params: \ell d+|\psi|\ \text{(encoder dropped after training, leaving } \ell d\text{)}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence, at arbitrary template positions interleaved with discrete anchor tokens
methods.structure: Virtual-token embeddings produced by a shared reparametrization network h=f_\psi(P) (bi-LSTM or MLP) that models dependencies between prompt tokens, inserted at template positions and concatenated with discrete prompt/anchor tokens.
methods.mergeable_reason: The continuous prompt tokens lengthen the input; only the encoder can be discarded (its outputs cached as embeddings).
methods.identity_at_init: No identity: the continuous prompt embeddings are freshly (randomly) initialized and concatenated with discrete prompt/anchor tokens, which the paper finds improves performance. The paper ablates LSTM, MLP and identity (EMB) prompt encoders and finds EMB unstable.
methods.key_idea: Make prompts continuous and let a small encoder couple the prompt tokens, which stabilizes training against the large variance of discrete prompts and lets GPT-style models compete with BERT-style models on NLU.
methods.results_note: With a frozen LM on LAMA knowledge probing P-Tuning beats manual prompts by 20+ points and searched prompts by 9 points; with tuned LMs it beats PET on SuperGLUE in both fully supervised and few-shot settings.

relations.note: Prompt tuning = P-Tuning with identity encoder and all virtual tokens at the front.
Both reparametrize prompt embeddings through a shared network; Residual PT adds a skip connection.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2103.10385 (Liu, Xiao; 2021-03) confirmed; journal version Crossref 10.1016/j.aiopen.2023.08.012 = AI Open vol. 5 (2024) pp. 208-215. Template T and prompt-encoder f (LSTM/MLP/identity) checked against Sec. 2.2-2.3 of v2. HF PromptEncoderConfig (MLP or LSTM reparametrization) confirmed.
corrections: url: pointed to the AI Open journal version (DOI confirmed via Crossref)
identity_at_init: removed the unsupported claim that training starts near the hand-written prompt; continuous prompts are new parameters concatenated with discrete tokens

methods.name: P-Tuning v2
methods.full_name: P-Tuning v2 (deep prompt tuning for NLU)
methods.paper_title: P-Tuning v2: Prompt Tuning Can Be Comparable to Fine-tuning Universally Across Scales and Tasks
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{head}^{(l)}=\mathrm{Attn}\big(XW_q^{(l)},\,[P_k^{(l)};XW_k^{(l)}],\,[P_v^{(l)};XW_v^{(l)}]\big)\ \ \forall l\le L,\quad \hat y=\mathrm{softmax}(W_{\mathrm{cls}}\,h_{\mathrm{tok}});\ \ P^{(l)}\ (\text{optionally } \mathrm{MLP}\text{-reparametrized}),\ W_{\mathrm{cls}}\ \text{trained};\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.locus: keys/values at every layer (deep prompts) plus a randomly initialized linear head on token representations
methods.structure: Learned key/value vectors prepended at every layer (identical parameter shape to prefix-tuning), with a linear classification head instead of a verbalizer, task-dependent prompt length (short for classification, ~100 for sequence labeling) and optional reparametrization / multitask initialization.
methods.mergeable_reason: Same as prefix-tuning: \ell extra key/value slots per layer that cannot be folded into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; random initialization, optionally a multitask-pretrained prompt as initialization.
methods.key_idea: Inserting prompts at every layer (not just the input) gives more capacity and more direct influence on predictions, making prompt tuning match fine-tuning even for 300M-scale models and for hard sequence-labeling tasks.
methods.results_note: Matches fine-tuning across model scales from 300M to 10B parameters and on hard sequence tagging (NER, extractive QA, SRL) while tuning 0.1%-3% of parameters.

relations.note: Self-described implementation of deep prompt tuning (Li & Liang 2021; Qin & Eisner 2021) adapted to NLU.
Prompt tuning is the input-layer-only special case.
Alternative PEFT method for NLU (not compared in the P-Tuning v2 paper; prefix-tuning vs. LoRA is compared by He et al. 2022).

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2110.07602 confirmed; published as ACL 2022 short paper 2022.acl-short.8 under the shortened title 'P-Tuning: Prompt Tuning Can Be Comparable to Fine-tuning Across Scales and Tasks'. HF has no separate P-Tuning v2 class: deep prompts are PrefixTuningConfig (its PrefixEncoder is adapted from THUDM/P-tuning-v2, and the PEFT v0.4.0 README listed P-Tuning v2 under Prefix Tuning); the linear classification head is not part of the PEFT config.

methods.name: WARP
methods.paper_title: WARP: Word-level Adversarial ReProgramming
methods.formula_latex: P_\Theta(y\mid x)=\frac{\exp\big(\Theta^{V}_{y}\cdot f(T_{\Theta^P}(x))\big)}{\sum_{i\in C}\exp\big(\Theta^{V}_{i}\cdot f(T_{\Theta^P}(x))\big)},\quad \Theta^P\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d}\ \text{(prompt embeddings inserted by template } T\text{ around a [MASK])},\ \Theta^V\in\mathbb{R}^{|C|\times d}\ \text{(verbalizer embeddings)}\ \text{trained; MLM body frozen}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence (template positions around a [MASK] token) and the output verbalizer vectors of the MLM head
methods.structure: Adversarial reprogramming in word-embedding space: learned input embeddings at template positions plus learned class vectors that replace output-embedding rows of the masked-LM head (an input-side and an output-side reprogramming map around a frozen body).
methods.mergeable_reason: Prompt embeddings lengthen the input; only the verbalizer vectors act like a (new) linear head.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; prompt tokens initialized with the [MASK] embedding or embeddings similar to the vocabulary; verbalizers from the MLM head.
methods.key_idea: Treat task adaptation as adversarial reprogramming: search continuous prompt and verbalizer embeddings by SGD so a frozen masked LM's [MASK] prediction solves the task.
methods.results_note: With up to 25K trainable parameters per task on RoBERTa-large it reaches 81.6 on the GLUE test leaderboard, beating submissions with up to three orders of magnitude more trainable parameters; strong few-shot SuperGLUE results with ALBERT.

relations.note: Concurrent continuous-prompt method; adds learned output verbalizers.
Same adversarial-reprogramming principle in text embedding space vs. pixel space.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2101.00121 and 2021.acl-long.381 confirmed; probability formula with f(T_{Theta^P}(x)) and verbalizer embeddings Theta^V checked against Sec. 3; initialization ([MASK] or word-like embeddings; verbalizers from the MLM head) checked in Sec. 3.2. Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: PPT
methods.paper_title: PPT: Pre-trained Prompt Tuning for Few-shot Learning
methods.formula_latex: P^\star=\arg\min_{P}\ \sum_{(X,Y)\in\mathcal{D}_{\text{self-sup}}}-\log\Pr_\theta\big(Y\mid[P;X]\big)\ \text{(unified pre-training tasks built from unlabeled text)};\ \ \text{then prompt tuning on the target task initialized at } P^\star;\ \theta\ \text{frozen throughout}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence
methods.structure: Vanilla soft prompt whose initialization is obtained by pre-training the prompt alone on self-supervised tasks cast in the same formats as downstream tasks (sentence-pair, multiple-choice, single-sentence classification, or a unified multiple-choice format).
methods.mergeable_reason: At inference it is an ordinary soft prompt that lengthens the input.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; the contribution is the initialization itself (a prompt pre-trained on the PLM's own pre-training-style objective).
methods.key_idea: Prompt tuning fails in few-shot regimes mainly because of poor initialization, so pre-train the soft prompt on large unlabeled corpora using task formats that mirror downstream classification.
methods.results_note: With T5-XXL and CPM-2 (~11B), tuning pre-trained prompts reaches or exceeds full-model fine-tuning in both full-data and few-shot settings, far above vanilla prompt tuning in few-shot.

relations.note: Same parameterization; adds prompt pre-training as initialization.
Self-supervised prompt pre-training versus supervised source-task transfer.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2109.04332 and 2022.acl-long.576 confirmed; the three pre-training formats and the unified multiple-choice format are in Sec. 3; results claim matches the abstract (full-data and few-shot). Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: SPoT
methods.paper_title: SPoT: Better Frozen Model Adaptation through Soft Prompt Transfer
methods.formula_latex: P_{s}=\arg\min_P\mathcal{L}_{s}\big([P;X]\big),\quad P_{t}^{(0)}\leftarrow P_{s^\star},\quad P_t^\star=\arg\min_P\mathcal{L}_{t}\big([P;X]\big);\ \ s^\star=\arg\max_s\cos\Big(\tfrac1\ell\textstyle\sum_i e^{s}_i,\ \tfrac1\ell\sum_j e^{t}_j\Big)\ \text{(early-checkpoint prompts as task embeddings; a per-token average cosine is the alternative metric)};\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence
methods.structure: Vanilla soft prompt initialized from a prompt trained on a source task (or multi-task mixture); early-checkpoint prompts double as task embeddings whose cosine similarity predicts transferability for source retrieval.
methods.mergeable_reason: At inference it is an ordinary soft prompt.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; initialization from a source-task prompt is the method.
methods.key_idea: Soft prompts are transferable task representations: train them on source tasks, use them to initialize target prompts, and use prompt similarity as a cheap task-similarity metric to choose sources.
methods.results_note: Across all T5 sizes, SPoT matches or outperforms full model tuning on SuperGLUE while using up to 27,000x fewer task-specific parameters; a 26-task, 160-pair transfer study shows widespread positive transfer.

relations.note: Same parameterization; adds source-to-target prompt initialization.
ATTEMPT mixes many source prompts per instance instead of picking one for initialization.
MPT distils many source prompts into one shared prompt.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2110.07904 and 2022.acl-long.346 confirmed; task similarity uses either the cosine of average-pooled prompt tokens (shown in the formula) or the per-token average cosine (Sec. 4); 27,000x and 26-task/160-pair figures confirmed. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: formula_latex: noted the paper's second similarity metric (per-token average cosine)

methods.name: ATTEMPT
methods.paper_title: ATTEMPT: Parameter-Efficient Multi-task Tuning via Attentional Mixtures of Soft Prompts
methods.formula_latex: P_{\mathrm{inst}}(X)=P_{\mathrm{tgt}}+\sum_{j=1}^{t+1}a_j(X)\,P_j,\quad a_j=\frac{\exp(\hat P_j^{\top}H_{\mathrm{out}}/T)}{\sum_{k=1}^{t+1}\exp(\hat P_k^{\top}H_{\mathrm{out}}/T)},\quad H_{\mathrm{out}}=\mathrm{LN}\big(W_{up}^{\top}\,\mathrm{SiLU}(W_{down}^{\top}\hat X)\big),\ P_{t+1}=P_{\mathrm{tgt}};\ \ \text{input }[P_{\mathrm{inst}}(X);X];\ \text{train } P_{\mathrm{tgt}},W_{down}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r},W_{up}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d};\ \text{source prompts } P_{1..t}\ \text{and LM frozen}
methods.trainable_params: d\big(\ell+2(r+1)/N\big)\ \text{per task (attention module shared across } N \text{ target tasks)}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence (instance-specific prompt)
methods.structure: Instance-wise softmax mixture (a point of the simplex) over a library of frozen source prompts plus the trainable target prompt, added to the target prompt; mixture weights come from a bottleneck network on the max-pooled input (\hat X, \hat P_j are max-pooled).
methods.mergeable_reason: The prompt depends on the input instance and lengthens the sequence; it can never be folded into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; source prompts pre-trained by prompt tuning on large source tasks, target prompt newly initialized.
methods.key_idea: Treat pre-trained soft prompts as modular knowledge units and learn, per input, an attention-weighted interpolation of them with a new target prompt, sharing the router across tasks.
methods.results_note: On 21 datasets with T5-base, significantly outperforms prompt tuning and matches or beats full fine-tuning and other PEFT methods that use over 10x more parameters, while updating ~2,300x fewer parameters than fine-tuning.

relations.note: SPoT picks one source prompt for initialization; ATTEMPT mixes all sources per instance.
Source and target prompts are vanilla soft prompts.
Alternative multitask prompt-transfer scheme.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2205.11961 and 2022.emnlp-main.446 confirmed; Eqs. (3)-(4), the max-pooled inputs, SiLU, LayerNorm, and the per-task parameter count d(m+2(r+1)/N) checked in Sec. 3.2-3.4. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: relations: removed 'l2p' (no head-to-head comparison or citation; different problem settings (multi-task NLP transfer vs. rehearsal-free continual learning), so 'competes-with' was unjustified)

methods.name: MPT
methods.paper_title: Multitask Prompt Tuning Enables Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning
methods.formula_latex: \hat P_k=P^{\ast}\circ\big(u_k v_k^{\top}\big),\quad P^{\ast}\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d}\ \text{shared},\ u_k\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell},\ v_k\in\mathbb{R}^{d};\ \ \text{source stage: } \min\ \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{PLM}}+\lambda\big(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Logits}}+\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hidden}}\big)\ \text{(distil per-task teacher prompts)};\ \ \text{target: train } P^{\ast},u_t,v_t;\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence
methods.structure: Hadamard product of a shared prompt matrix with a task-specific rank-one matrix (a multiplicative rank-1 modulation of a shared prompt), the shared factor learned by multitask knowledge distillation from per-task teacher prompts.
methods.mergeable_reason: After training P^\ast\circ(u v^\top) collapses to one \ell\times d prompt, but it still lengthens the input.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; the target prompt is initialized from the distilled shared prompt (HF options: AVERAGE_SOURCE_TASKS, EXACT_SOURCE_TASK, ONLY_SOURCE_SHARED, TEXT, RANDOM).
methods.key_idea: Decompose task prompts into shared 'slow' knowledge and a cheap task-specific rank-one multiplicative 'fast' factor, distil many source prompts into the shared part, then adapt only that to targets.
methods.results_note: On 23 NLP datasets, outperforms state-of-the-art PEFT methods, and full fine-tuning in some cases, while tuning only 0.035% as many task-specific parameters.

relations.note: Prompt transfer from source tasks, made multiplicative and multitask.
Distils sources into one prompt instead of mixing them per instance.
Teacher prompts and inference format are vanilla prompt tuning.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2303.02861 confirmed; OpenReview Nk2pDtuhTq = ICLR 2023 poster. Decomposition P_k = P* o (u_k v_k^T), distillation loss L_PLM + lambda(L_Logits + L_Hidden), and (l x d)+(l+d) target parameters checked in Sec. 3. HF MultitaskPromptTuningConfig confirmed (init options TEXT, RANDOM, AVERAGE_SOURCE_TASKS, EXACT_SOURCE_TASK, ONLY_SOURCE_SHARED). No official code found (project page only).

methods.name: DePT
methods.paper_title: DePT: Decomposed Prompt Tuning for Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning
methods.formula_latex: \text{input } \big[P_s;\ E_X+AB\big],\quad P_s\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell'\times d},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times r},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d},\ E_X\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times d}\ \text{frozen word embeddings of the input padded to the maximum length } s;\ \ \ell' d+(s+d)r=\ell d;\ \ A\sim\mathcal{N},\ B=0;\ \text{learning rates } \alpha_1(P_s)\gg\alpha_2(A,B);\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence: a shorter soft prompt plus a position-wise offset to the input token embeddings
methods.structure: Short soft prompt (concatenation) plus a rank-r additive, position-indexed offset AB to the frozen s\times d input-embedding matrix, i.e. a LoRA-style low-rank update applied to the input activation matrix rather than to a weight (the paper writes the product as BA; dimensionally it is the s\times d matrix A B).
methods.mergeable_reason: The short prompt still lengthens the input; the positional offset AB could only be folded into absolute position embeddings, which T5-style relative-position models lack.
methods.identity_at_init: The low-rank offset is zero at init (B=0); the short prompt is not an identity.
methods.key_idea: Trade prompt length for a low-rank update of the input embeddings: same parameter budget, shorter sequences, so lower time/memory, trained with two learning rates.
methods.results_note: Across 23 NLP and vision-language tasks, outperforms vanilla prompt tuning and other PEFT methods (sometimes full fine-tuning) while saving over 20% training/inference time and memory relative to prompt tuning with T5-Base.

relations.note: Splits the prompt budget between a shorter prompt and a low-rank embedding offset.
Imports the BA low-rank, zero-initialized update, applied to the input embedding matrix.
Both are low-rank prompt decompositions evaluated on the same 23-task suite.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2309.05173 confirmed, ICLR 2024 per arXiv comment. Eq. (2) is written W_i + BA with A in R^{s x r}, B in R^{r x d}; dimensionally the s x d update is AB (kept). Budget l x d = m x d + (s+d) x r, Gaussian A / zero B, and two learning rates checked in Sec. 2.2. Code repo moved to github.com/ShiZhengyan/DePT. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: formula_latex: s is the maximum (padded) sequence length in the paper, not the length of a given input
code_url: repository was renamed; GitHub redirects ZhengxiangShi/DePT to ShiZhengyan/DePT

methods.name: Residual Prompt Tuning
methods.paper_title: Residual Prompt Tuning: Improving Prompt Tuning with Residual Reparameterization
methods.formula_latex: P'_i=\Phi(P_i)=\mathrm{LN}\big(\mathrm{ReLU}(P_iW_{down})\,W_{up}\big)+P_i,\ \ i=1,\dots,\ell\ \ (P_i\ \text{a row vector});\ \ \text{input }[P';X];\ \ \text{train } P\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d},\ W_{down}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times m},\ W_{up}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d},\ \mathrm{LN};\ \text{after training store only } P'=\Phi(P);\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \ell d+2dm+2d\ \text{(training: prompt, } W_{down},W_{up}\text{ and LayerNorm, as counted in the paper)};\ \ \ell d\ \text{(stored)}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence
methods.structure: Soft prompt reparametrized through a shared bottleneck MLP with LayerNorm and a residual skip, applied token-wise; the reparametrization is discarded after training (an over-parameterization that only changes the optimization geometry).
methods.mergeable_reason: At inference only the projected prompt P' remains, which still lengthens the input.
methods.identity_at_init: No model-level identity; the residual skip lets each virtual token choose between its free embedding and the shared projection, improving robustness to learning rate and initialization.
methods.key_idea: Prompt tuning is unstable because prompt tokens are optimized independently; a shared residual MLP couples them and speeds and stabilizes training at no inference cost.
methods.results_note: Significantly outperforms prompt tuning on SuperGLUE with T5-Large, T5-Base and BERT-Base (e.g., +7 points with T5-Base), allows 10x shorter prompts without loss, and helps in few-shot settings.

relations.note: Same inference-time object; different training parameterization.
Prompt-encoder reparametrization, with an added skip connection.
Inherits the MLP-reparametrization trick used for prefixes.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2305.03937 and 2023.findings-acl.421 confirmed. Paper writes W_down in R^{d x m}, W_up in R^{m x d} (row-vector convention) and counts 2dm+2d reparametrization parameters (Appendix A.6). Baselines include PT w/ MLP (Li & Liang) and PT w/ LSTM (P-Tuning), SPoT and ATTEMPT. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: formula_latex: matched the paper's shapes W_down in R^{d x m}, W_up in R^{m x d} (row-vector convention) and listed the trainable LayerNorm
trainable_params: added the 2d LayerNorm parameters counted in the paper (Appendix A.6)

methods.name: LPT
methods.paper_title: Late Prompt Tuning: A Late Prompt Could Be Better Than Many Prompts
methods.formula_latex: h^{(l^\ast)}\leftarrow\big[p(x);\,h^{(l^\ast)}\big],\quad p(x)=W_2\,\mathrm{ReLU}\big(\mathrm{Pool}_{n\to\ell}(W_1h^{(l^\ast)}+b_1)\big)+b_2\ \ (\text{pooling generator}),\ \ \text{or}\ \ p(x)=\mathrm{Reshape}\big(W_2\,\mathrm{ReLU}(W_1h_{[\mathrm{CLS}]}+b_1)+b_2\big)\ (\text{naive});\ \ W_1\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d};\ \text{single insertion layer } l^\ast\ (\text{e.g. 13 of 24});\ \text{backbone frozen}
methods.locus: hidden-state sequence at a single intermediate layer
methods.structure: Instance-dependent prompt generated by a bottleneck MLP (with optional pooling from input length n to prompt length ℓ) from the hidden states just below the insertion layer, inserted once at an intermediate layer.
methods.mergeable_reason: The prompt is input-dependent and adds tokens to the upper half of the network.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity.
methods.key_idea: There is a trade-off between how far the label signal must propagate back to the prompt and how much the prompt can influence outputs; a single 'late' prompt in a middle layer, generated from the instance's own hidden states, balances both and skips backprop through the lower layers.

methods.paper_title: Black-Box Tuning for Language-Model-as-a-Service

methods.mergeable_reason: The result is a soft prompt that lengthens the input.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; z=0 gives the initial prompt p_0.

methods.name: CPT
methods.paper_title: Context-aware Prompt Tuning: Advancing In-Context Learning with Adversarial Methods
methods.formula_latex: X_{\mathrm{Train}_i}=\big[X_{\mathrm{Context}};\,X_{\mathrm{Emb}_i}\big],\ X_{\mathrm{Context}}=[X_{\mathrm{Emb}_1};\dots;X_{\mathrm{Emb}_N}]+\delta;\quad \min_{\delta}\ \sum_{k=1}^{N}\gamma^{\,N+1-k}\,\mathrm{CE}\big(\hat t^{(k)}_{O},t^{(k)}_{O}\big)+\mathrm{CE}\big(\hat t^{(N+1)}_{O},t^{(N+1)}_{O}\big)\ \ \text{s.t. } \|\delta_j\|_2\le\epsilon\ \text{per token (projected GD)};\ \text{label tokens of the context not updated; LM frozen}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence (the embedded in-context demonstrations)
methods.structure: In-context demonstrations used as a soft prompt: the input/format token embeddings of the N few-shot examples are optimized inside per-token \ell_2 balls of radius \epsilon around their original embeddings (adversarial-style PGD, but minimizing loss), with all context labels in the loss and exponentially decayed weights toward the start of the context.
methods.mergeable_reason: The optimized context occupies the input window exactly like in-context examples.
methods.identity_at_init: Initialized at the exact embeddings of the user's demonstrations (\delta=0), i.e. plain in-context learning; \epsilon\to0 recovers ICL.
methods.key_idea: Combine in-context learning with prompt tuning: refine the embeddings of the demonstrations themselves, but keep them close to the user's examples (projection) and supervise every in-context label, to avoid few-shot overfitting.
methods.results_note: In few-shot classification (SST-2, AG News, DBpedia, TREC and a new Set Classification task) with models such as GPT-J 6B, Llama-3 8B and BLOOM-1.7B, reports higher accuracy than ICL, prompt tuning, instruction prompt tuning and LoRA baselines.

methods.name: LLaMA-Adapter
methods.paper_title: LLaMA-Adapter: Efficient Fine-tuning of Language Models with Zero-init Attention

methods.structure: Layer-wise learned prompts entering only through the frozen key/value projections, attended with their own softmax and scaled by a zero-initialized tanh gate; because the content softmax is kept separate, the result is the original attention plus an additive gated prefix branch \tanh(g_l)\,\mathrm{softmax}(S^{K}_l)P_lW_v.

methods.identity_at_init: Exact: g_l=0 gives \tanh(g_l)=0, so the prompt branch contributes nothing and the separately normalized content attention is untouched.

methods.name: VPT
methods.paper_title: Visual Prompt Tuning
methods.formula_latex: \text{Shallow: } [x_1,Z_1,E_1]=L_1([x_0,P,E_0]),\ [x_i,Z_i,E_i]=L_i([x_{i-1},Z_{i-1},E_{i-1}]);\quad \text{Deep: } [x_i,\_\,,E_i]=L_i([x_{i-1},P_{i-1},E_{i-1}]),\ i=1,\dots,L;\quad y=\mathrm{Head}(x_L);\ \ P,P_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d}\ \text{and Head trained; ViT frozen}

methods.name: Visual Prompting

methods.formula_latex: \max_{\phi}\ \log P_{\theta;\phi}\big(y\mid x+v_\phi\big),\quad v_\phi\ \text{a single pixel-space perturbation shared by all images (padding frame of width } p\text{, or a patch)};\ \ \theta\ \text{frozen; labels via CLIP text prompts}

methods.structure: An additive translation of input space, x\mapsto x+v_\phi, supported on a border frame (or a patch).

methods.key_idea: Adapt a frozen vision model by learning a single input perturbation (adversarial reprogramming as prompting), with the output mapped to labels through text prompts for CLIP.

relations.note: Adversarial reprogramming lineage, in pixel space.
Pixel-space prompts vs. token-space prompts.
Image-side vs. text-side learned prompting of a frozen CLIP for the same classification task (not compared head-to-head in Bahng et al.).

methods.name: CoOp
methods.paper_title: Learning to Prompt for Vision-Language Models
methods.formula_latex: t_i=[V]_1[V]_2\cdots[V]_{\ell}[\mathrm{CLASS}_i],\qquad p(y=i\mid x)=\frac{\exp\big(\cos(g(t_i),f(x))/\tau\big)}{\sum_{j=1}^{K}\exp\big(\cos(g(t_j),f(x))/\tau\big)};\ \ [V]_m\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\ \text{trained (unified or class-specific)};\ \text{CLIP encoders } f,g\ \text{frozen}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence of the CLIP text encoder
methods.structure: Soft prompt (shared or per-class context vectors) prepended to each class-name token sequence; the classifier weights are the frozen text encoder's images g(t_i) of the prompted class names.
methods.mergeable_reason: In closed-set classification the K prompted class embeddings g(t_i) are computed once after training and cached as a linear classifier, so inference costs exactly as much as zero-shot CLIP; the learned context itself cannot be folded into the text encoder's weights, and any new class name requires re-running the text encoder with the prompt.
methods.identity_at_init: Can be initialized from the embedding of a hand-crafted context such as 'a photo of a' (starting at the zero-shot classifier) or randomly.
methods.key_idea: Replace hand-engineered CLIP prompts by learnable context vectors optimized end-to-end through the frozen text encoder.
methods.results_note: On 11 image-recognition datasets, one or two shots suffice to beat hand-crafted prompts, and with 16 shots the average gain is around 15%.

relations.note: Prompt tuning applied to the text tower of a contrastive vision-language model.
CoCoOp with the meta-net output fixed to zero.

methods.name: CoCoOp
methods.paper_title: Conditional Prompt Learning for Vision-Language Models
methods.formula_latex: v_m(x)=v_m+h_\theta\big(f(x)\big),\ \ t_i(x)=\{v_1(x),\dots,v_\ell(x),c_i\},\qquad p(y\mid x)=\frac{\exp\big(\mathrm{sim}(f(x),g(t_y(x)))/\tau\big)}{\sum_{i=1}^{K}\exp\big(\mathrm{sim}(f(x),g(t_i(x)))/\tau\big)};\ \ h_\theta=\text{Linear-ReLU-Linear (16}\times\text{ bottleneck)};\ \text{train } v_{1..\ell},\theta;\ \text{CLIP frozen}

methods.structure: Context vectors shifted by one image-conditioned token π=h_θ(f(x)) produced by a lightweight meta-network (an input-dependent translation of the shared prompt).
methods.mergeable_reason: Class embeddings depend on the image, so the text encoder must be re-run for all K classes per image (much higher inference cost than CoOp).
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; reduces to CoOp when h_θ outputs zero.
methods.key_idea: Static learned prompts overfit to base classes; making the prompt conditional on each image improves generalization to unseen classes and domains.
methods.results_note: Generalizes much better than CoOp to unseen classes within a dataset, and improves cross-dataset transfer and domain generalization across 11 datasets.

relations.note: Adds an instance-conditional shift to CoOp's context vectors.

methods.name: MaPLe
methods.paper_title: MaPLe: Multi-modal Prompt Learning

methods.name: Cartridges
methods.paper_title: Cartridges: Lightweight and general-purpose long context representations via self-study
methods.formula_latex: \text{KV}^{(l)}=\big[(z_k^{(l)}[1],z_v^{(l)}[1]),\dots,(z_k^{(l)}[\ell],z_v^{(l)}[\ell]);\ (k^{(l)}[q],v^{(l)}[q])\big],\ \ Z\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times\ell\times d\times 2}\ \text{trained directly (no reparametrization)};\quad \min_{Z}\ \mathbb{E}\ \mathrm{KL}\Big(F(\cdot\mid\tilde c\oplus q)\ \big\|\ F_Z(\cdot\mid q)\Big)\ \text{on synthetic Self-Study conversations about corpus } \mathcal{C};\ \text{LLM frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 2L\ell d\ \ (d=\text{per-layer key/value width; } 2L(\ell-1)d \text{ trainable when the first (attention-sink) token is frozen})
methods.locus: keys/values at every layer (a trained KV cache)
methods.structure: A learned initial KV-cache state: prefix-tuning without the MLP reparametrization, initialized from the true prefill KV of the first \ell corpus tokens and trained by context distillation against the model with the (sub)corpus in context.
methods.mergeable_reason: It is served as an \ell-token cached prefix (no custom kernels needed) but cannot be folded into the weights.
methods.identity_at_init: No exact identity; initialized to the KV cache of the first \ell tokens of the corpus (a truncated-context model), with the first token frozen as an attention sink for stability (HF num_frozen_tokens=1).
methods.key_idea: Instead of placing a long corpus in context, train a small KV cache offline per corpus with a self-generated, context-distillation objective; amortize the cost over all queries.
methods.results_note: On long-context benchmarks, matches ICL quality while using 38.6x less memory and enabling 26.4x higher throughput, extends effective context (128k to 484k tokens on MTOB), and independently trained cartridges compose at inference.

relations.note: Self-described simplified prefix-tuning (direct KV parameterization); new objective and initialization.
The paper finds KV-cache parameterization beats a LoRA parameterization for this use.
Transformer counterpart of learning the recurrence's initial state.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2506.06266 confirmed; ICLR 2026 poster (OpenReview 0k5w8O0SNg). Parameterization Z in R^{L x p x d x 2} (simplified prefix-tuning), KL context-distillation objective, initialization from the first p corpus tokens and frozen attention-sink token checked in Sec. 3-5; 38.6x memory / 26.4x throughput / 128k->484k MTOB confirmed in the abstract. HF CartridgeConfig (num_frozen_tokens=1 default) confirmed in peft main.

methods.name: Initial State Tuning
methods.full_name: Initial State Tuning (for state space models)
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of State Space Models
methods.formula_latex: h_t=\bar A_t h_{t-1}+\bar B_t x_t,\ \ y_t=C_th_t\ \ \text{run from } h_0=h'\ \text{instead of } 0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \hat y_t=y_t+C_t\Big(\prod_{i=1}^{t}\bar A_i\Big)h',\quad h'\in\mathbb{R}^{H}\ \text{per channel trained; all SSM weights frozen}
methods.locus: initial hidden state of each SSM (e.g. Mamba S6) layer
methods.structure: Learned initial state of a linear recurrence. On S4, any prefix of virtual tokens acts only through h_{\mathrm{prefix}}=\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}\bar A^{i}\bar Bx_{-i}, so prefix-tuning is exactly an initial-state update (Prop. 1); conversely every initial state is realizable by a prefix iff \ell\ge H (under a genericity condition).
methods.mergeable_reason: No weight changes and per-token cost is unchanged, since SSM scan kernels accept an initial state natively, but the state is injected per sequence (in S6 its effect C_t(\prod_i\bar A_i)h' is input-dependent) and cannot be folded into W_0, exactly like a cached prefix.
methods.identity_at_init: h'=0 recovers the base model exactly.
methods.key_idea: For SSMs, the whole effect of prompt/prefix tuning is captured by the initial hidden state, so tune that state directly: an upper bound on prefix-tuning's expressivity at the same cost.
methods.results_note: On Mamba with <0.5% trainable parameters, initial state tuning outperforms prefix-tuning and prompt tuning on five of seven tasks, but LoRA consistently outperforms it.

relations.note: Galim et al. Prop. 1: on S4 every prefix acts as an initial-state update; the converse holds iff the prefix length is at least H (genericity assumption), so initial-state tuning upper-bounds prefix-tuning.
State-offset tuning removes the decaying coefficient ∏ A_i.
LoRA outperforms state-based tuning in Galim et al.'s benchmarks.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.09016 confirmed (ICML 2025 per arXiv comment). Prop. 1 (S4): every prefix equals an initial-state update, converse iff M >= H under a genericity assumption; initial-state tuning results in Table 14 (beats prefix/prompt tuning on 5 of 7 GLUE tasks, LoRA better). The S6 output formula with prod_i A_i is the form given in Kang et al. (2025) Table 1. Mergeability changed to no for consistency with prefix-tuning and Cartridges. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: mergeable: a learned recurrence state is served like a cached prefix and is not folded into any weight; prefix-type methods are non-mergeable in this catalog
mergeable_reason: rewritten to match the corrected mergeable value
relations[prefix-tuning]: type changed equivalent-to -> generalizes: Prop. 1 gives only one inclusion in general (prefix => initial state), with equality iff prefix length >= H

methods.name: State-offset Tuning
methods.paper_title: State-offset Tuning: State-based Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for State Space Models
methods.formula_latex: \hat y_t=y_t+C_t\,h'\ \ \text{(State-offset (h))},\qquad \hat y_t=y_t+y'\ \ \text{(State-offset (y))},\qquad h'\in\mathbb{R}^{H}\ \text{per channel},\ y'\in\mathbb{R}^{D};\ \text{SSM weights frozen}
methods.trainable_params: DH\ \text{(h variant)};\ \ D\ \text{(y variant) per SSM layer}
methods.locus: state readout at every timestep of each SSM (Mamba S6) layer
methods.structure: A constant learned offset added to the hidden state before readout at every step (Initial State Tuning with the time-varying factor \prod_i\bar A_i removed). In S6, C_th'=(W_Cx_t)^\top h', so the h-variant is a rank-\le H linear term in x_t; the y-variant is a bias on the SSM output.
methods.mergeable_reason: The offset enters before Mamba's multiplicative output gate (and as a linear term in x_t for the h-variant), so it cannot be absorbed into the existing diagonal skip or biases, although its cost is negligible.
methods.identity_at_init: h'=0 (or y'=0) recovers the frozen model exactly; the official code supports zero or Kaiming-uniform initialization of the offset parameters.
methods.key_idea: State-based PEFT for SSMs: instead of injecting external virtual tokens, add a learnable constant to the internal state at every timestep, giving a uniform rather than decaying effect.
methods.results_note: On Mamba-family models, State-offset Tuning (h) outperforms prompt-, prefix- and initial-state tuning and BitFit, and surpasses LoRA on most datasets; the (y) variant beats initial state tuning with 0.01% vs 0.23% of parameters.

relations.note: Removes the time-varying coefficient of the initial-state term.
Prompt-based methods underperform state-based ones on SSMs.
The y-variant is bias-like; reported to outperform BitFit.
Surpasses LoRA on most reported datasets.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2503.03499 confirmed (ACL 2025 Main per arXiv comment). Table 1 formulas y_t + C_t h' (h variant, DH params) and y_t + y' (y variant, D params) checked; 0.01% vs 0.23% parameter claim confirmed; BitFit and LoRA are baselines. Official code offers zero or Kaiming-uniform init for the offset parameters. Not in HF PEFT.

papers.title: Towards a Unified View of Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning
papers.claim: Prefix-tuning is exactly rewritten as h \leftarrow (1-\lambda(x))h+\lambda(x)\,\mathrm{softmax}(xW_qP_k^\top)P_v, a gated parallel adapter; adapters, prefix-tuning and LoRA become instances of one template (modified representation, insertion form, functional form, composition function).
papers.relevance: Supplies the key morphism between the prompt family and the adapter family: a prefix is a parallel adapter with softmax nonlinearity, input-dependent gate and K/V-shaped weights; the composition functions (gated, plain, scaled addition) are natural candidates for categorical structure.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2110.04366 (He, Junxian; 2021-10) confirmed; ICLR 2022 spotlight per arXiv comment; gated-adapter rewrite of prefix-tuning matches Sec. 3.

papers.title: When Do Prompting and Prefix-Tuning Work? A Theory of Capabilities and Limitations
papers.claim: Soft prompting and prefix-tuning can be strictly less expressive than full fine-tuning with the same parameter count: they cannot change the relative attention pattern over the content and can only bias attention-layer outputs in a fixed direction, so they elicit existing skills rather than learn tasks needing new attention patterns.
papers.relevance: Characterizes the image of the prompt family inside the space of model modifications (an expressivity limit), essential for placing prompts in a hierarchy against weight-space methods.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2310.19698 confirmed; ICLR 2024 poster (OpenReview JewzobRhay); claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Universality and Limitations of Prompt Tuning
papers.claim: There exists a transformer for which prompts approximate any Lipschitz sequence-to-sequence function; conversely, for a given single encoder layer there are datasets that no prompt of any length can memorize, with a lower bound on prompt parameters compared against a LoRA update in the single-layer setting, and sufficient conditions in the multi-layer case under which only invertible functions can be learned.
papers.relevance: Gives both a universality (density) statement and an obstruction for prompt tuning, and a direct parameter-count comparison with low-rank weight updates.
corrections: claim: the memorization impossibility is proved for a given single encoder layer, not for general finite-depth transformers; added the multi-layer invertibility result

papers.title: Prompting a Pretrained Transformer Can Be a Universal Approximator
papers.claim: Prefix-tuning a single attention head suffices to approximate any continuous function, and any sequence-to-sequence function can be approximated by prefixing a transformer of depth linear in the sequence length, with Jackson-type bounds on the required prefix length.
papers.relevance: Complements the limitation results: the prompt family is universal for suitably chosen (even small) pretrained models, so its expressivity depends on the frozen backbone, a functorial dependence worth formalizing.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2402.14753 confirmed; ICML 2024, PMLR v235 petrov24a.
corrections: url: pointed to the PMLR proceedings page (confirmed)

papers.title: On the Role of Attention in Prompt-tuning
papers.claim: In one-layer attention models on contextual mixture data, softmax prompt-attention is provably more expressive than softmax self-attention and linear prompt-attention; gradient descent learns the prompt with near-optimal sample complexity and the prompt attends to sparse context-relevant tokens.
papers.relevance: Isolates the attention mechanism as the channel through which prompts act, with learning-theoretic guarantees.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2306.03435 confirmed; ICML 2023, PMLR v202 oymak23a.
corrections: url: pointed to the PMLR proceedings page (confirmed)

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of State Space Models
papers.claim: For S4, any prefix acts on the outputs only through an initial hidden state, so prefix-tuning is upper-bounded by initial-state tuning, with equality iff the prefix length is at least the state size H (under a genericity assumption); prompt-based methods are therefore weak on SSMs, LoRA works best on linear projections, and Sparse Dimension Tuning (SDT) is proposed for SSM modules.
papers.relevance: A clean theorem embedding the prompt family into the 'learned initial state' family: on SSMs, prompts are points of the state space the recurrence starts from (all of it once \ell \ge H).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.09016 confirmed; ICML 2025 per arXiv comment; Prop. 1 and SDT ('Sparse Dimension Tuning' in the current version) checked.
corrections: claim: stated Prop. 1 as one inclusion plus a conditional converse rather than plain equivalence
relevance: 'identifying' overstated Prop. 1; it is an embedding that is onto only when the prefix length is at least H

papers.title: Revisiting Prefix-tuning: Statistical Benefits of Reparameterization among Prompts
papers.claim: The MLP reparametrization in prefix-tuning implicitly shares structure between prefix keys and values; via the prefix-tuning/mixture-of-experts connection this shared structure provably improves sample efficiency of parameter estimation, with similar benefits for prompt tuning.
papers.relevance: Explains why training-time reparametrizations (prefix MLP, P-Tuning encoder, Residual PT) matter even though they vanish at inference: they change the statistical geometry, not the hypothesis class.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.02200 confirmed; ICLR 2025 poster (OpenReview QjTSaFXg25); claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Exploring Universal Intrinsic Task Subspace via Prompt Tuning
papers.claim: Soft prompts of 100 NLP tasks can be decomposed into a shared 250-dimensional nonlinear subspace; tuning only 250 free parameters recovers 97% (seen tasks) and 83% (20 unseen tasks) of full prompt-tuning performance.
papers.relevance: Empirical evidence that the 'space of task adaptations' reachable by prompts is low-dimensional and shared, motivating a moduli-space view of PEFT.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2110.07867 confirmed. arXiv comment says it was previously accepted to Findings of ACL 2022 and Findings of EMNLP 2022; final version published in IEEE/ACM TASLP vol. 32 (2024) pp. 3631-3643, DOI 10.1109/TASLP.2024.3430545, as 'Exploring Universal Intrinsic Task Subspace for Few-Shot Learning via Prompt Tuning'.

papers.title: On Transferability of Prompt Tuning for Natural Language Processing
papers.claim: Soft prompts transfer zero-shot to similar tasks on the same PLM and, through a trained cross-model projector, to other PLMs; as initialization they accelerate and improve prompt tuning; the overlap rate of activated neurons predicts transferability better than embedding similarity.
papers.relevance: Treats prompts as transportable objects between tasks and between models (a projector is literally a map between prompt spaces of different backbones).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2111.06719 and ACL Anthology 2022.naacl-main.290 confirmed; claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Prompt Waywardness: The Curious Case of Discretized Interpretation of Continuous Prompts
papers.claim: Continuous prompts can solve a task while their nearest-neighbour discrete projection is arbitrary text (even a contradictory task definition), within ~2% of the best prompt's accuracy; the effect grows with model size.
papers.relevance: Shows that the map from continuous prompts back to discrete text is far from faithful: soft prompts live outside the image of the vocabulary embedding, so 'discrete prompting' is a thin subobject of the prompt space.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2112.08348 and ACL Anthology 2022.naacl-main.266 confirmed; claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large-scale pre-trained language models
papers.claim: Surveys 'delta tuning' and proposes a three-way taxonomy (addition-based, including prompts and prefixes; specification-based; reparameterization-based), with optimization and optimal-control perspectives and a large empirical study.
papers.relevance: The canonical prior taxonomy that a categorical reconstruction should refine; prompt methods sit in its addition-based class.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2203.06904 (titled 'Delta Tuning: A Comprehensive Study of Parameter Efficient Methods for Pre-trained Language Models') confirmed; journal version Nature Machine Intelligence 5:220-235 (2023), DOI 10.1038/s42256-023-00626-4, whose title is the one used here.

papers.title: Pre-train, Prompt, and Predict: A Systematic Survey of Prompting Methods in Natural Language Processing
papers.claim: Systematizes prompt-based learning (templates, answer spaces, discrete and continuous prompts, tuning strategies such as fixed-LM prompt tuning and prompt+LM tuning).
papers.relevance: Standard reference for the discrete/continuous prompt landscape and its notation.

papers.title: Inducer-tuning: Connecting Prefix-tuning and Adapter-tuning
papers.claim: Interprets prefixes as inducing variables of a kernel estimator in attention and proposes inducer-tuning, which keeps prefix-tuning's mechanism but uses an adapter-style residual form to fix prefix initialization.
papers.relevance: A second, kernel-theoretic bridge between the prompt and adapter families (low citation count, kept for its structural content).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2210.14469 and ACL Anthology 2022.emnlp-main.50 confirmed; claim matches the abstract.

notes: Scope: soft prompts, prefixes / deep prompts, prompt transfer, decomposition and multitask prompts, instance-conditional prompts, vision and vision-language prompt learning, prompt pools for continual learning, and the learned-state family (trained KV caches, SSM initial-state and state-offset tuning). All seed methods were confirmed and kept. Formulas were checked against each paper's method section (PDF full text); notation adapted to \ell (prompt length), d, L. Structural facts useful for a categorical treatment: (1) Li & Liang's expressivity chain discrete prompt < embedding-only (prompt tuning) < prefix-tuning; (2) He et al. 2022: prefix-tuning = gated parallel adapter; (3) VPT-Deep and LLaMA-Adapter are prefixes tied through the frozen LN/W_k/W_v (VPT tie derived here from the paper's equations); (4) P-Tuning v2 is the same parameter object as prefix-tuning; Cartridges are prefix-tuning without reparametrization; (5) on S4 SSMs a prefix acts only through the initial state, so initial-state tuning upper-bounds prefix-tuning, with equality iff \ell >= H (Galim et al. Prop. 1); (6) training-time reparametrizations (prefix MLP, P-Tuning LSTM/MLP, Residual PT, BBT random subspace) change optimization/statistics but not the inference-time object (Le et al. 2025). Derived (not in source papers, flagged in fields): mergeability of pixel-space visual prompting into ViT positional embeddings; S6 state-offset as a linear term in x_t; CoOp class embeddings cacheable. Uncertainties: CPT has no formal venue (ICLR 2025 and TMLR rejections, ARR 2025 submission on OpenReview; a web search claim of ICLR 2025 acceptance was wrong), recorded as arXiv. Initial State Tuning is attributed to Galim et al. (2024; ICML 2025) as stated by the State-offset paper; the idea of a learned initial RNN state is older. MPT has no official code release found (HF PEFT MultitaskPromptTuningConfig is the reference implementation). IDPG/XPrompt code not found. HF PEFT (v0.21.1, 2026-09-29) prompt-type tuners: PromptTuningConfig, PrefixTuningConfig, PromptEncoderConfig, MultitaskPromptTuningConfig, AdaptionPromptConfig, CPTConfig, CartridgeConfig; note HF applies prefix-tuning only to the decoder for seq2seq models, and its init_weights='zero' is not an exact identity. Omitted (lower uptake or better placed elsewhere): HF TrainableTokens (selective family), ReFT/RED-style representation interventions (activation-editing family), CODA-Prompt, PromptSRC, KgCoOp, ProGrad, E2VPT, HyperPrompt (tunes the whole model), SMoP, Adaptive Prefix Tuning, Prefix-Propagation, Gisting (fine-tunes the LM), Instruction Prompt Tuning, LLaMA-Adapter V2.
verification_summary: Adversarial check on 2026-10-01 of all 27 methods and 13 papers. Metadata: all 39 arXiv ids were fetched from arxiv.org/abs pages (the export API returned 503); titles, first authors and first-version years all match. Venues were confirmed through arXiv comments, ACL Anthology pages (14 ids), PMLR pages, OpenReview (MPT ICLR 2023, Wang NeurIPS 2023, Petrov ICLR 2024, LLaMA-Adapter ICLR 2024, Le ICLR 2025, Cartridges ICLR 2026) and Crossref (AI Open, IJCV, NMI, ACM CSUR, TASLP). One venue was changed: Qin et al. was arXiv and is now IEEE/ACM TASLP 2024. CPT has no formal venue (ICLR 2025 rejected, ARR 2025 submission) and Visual Prompting has none, so both stay arXiv. Formulas were checked against the PDF full text of every method paper; no parametrization was wrong. Fixes: Residual PT shapes and LN parameters; DePT's s is the maximum sequence length; parameter-count clarifications for prefix-tuning, IDPG (+head), DualPrompt and Cartridges (frozen sink token); VPT storage 0.53%. Mergeability: CoOp yes -> conditional (only the cached closed-set classifier, the prompt is not foldable); Initial State Tuning conditional -> no (a learned state, like a cached prefix). Visual Prompting identity_at_init: the official code initializes randn, so there is no identity at init. HF PEFT (main, v0.21.1, tuners dir listed via GitHub API): PromptTuningConfig, PrefixTuningConfig (also covers P-Tuning v2), PromptEncoderConfig, MultitaskPromptTuningConfig, AdaptionPromptConfig, CPTConfig and CartridgeConfig all confirmed; no other method here is supported. Relations: removed 5 unjustified ones (attempt<->l2p, cocoop->idpg, xprompt->residual-prompt-tuning, cpt->warp) and retyped 3 (prefix-tuning/initial-state-tuning as special-case-of/generalizes per Galim Prop. 1; vpt->p-tuning-v2 builds-on). Target 'mezo' is a canonical slug that is not defined in any family file yet. Nothing was dropped. 39 field-level corrections were made in total.
